images.title: Big triangle minus small triangle
images.purpose: Shows the obtuse triangle ABC as the right triangle ADC with the right triangle ADB taken away.
images.composition: One right triangle ADC, large and centred, with the obtuse triangle ABC highlighted inside it.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. Points on a horizontal line: D at 0, B at 3 units right of D, C at 9 units right of D. A is 4 units directly above D. Triangle ABC (A to B, B to C, C to A) is filled teal (#0072B2). Triangle ADB (A to D, D to B, B to A) is filled amber (#E69F00). A grey (#6B7280) dashed segment from D to B shows CB extended, and a grey dashed vertical segment AD is the height, with a small right angle mark at D. Labels: A, B, C, D at those points; 4 cm beside AD; 3 cm under DB; 6 cm under BC; 12 cm² inside the teal triangle. Check: DC = 9, 1/2 × 4 × 9 = 18, 1/2 × 4 × 3 = 6, 18 − 6 = 12 = 1/2 × 4 × 6.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The height can fall outside, and 1/2 × base × height still gives 12 cm².
images.description: Shows the obtuse triangle ABC as the right triangle ADC with the right triangle ADB taken away.
images.context: Matches the worked example: h = 4 cm, DB = 3 cm, BC = 6 cm, area 12 cm².
images.teaching_notes: Cover the amber piece with a hand: what is left is the teal triangle.

image_decisions.why: The subtraction of one right triangle from another is a visual step; the outside height must be seen.
